Games: winning positions computed backwards from the end; a first draft that needs every play to end and closes on a question (does move-by-move induction reach every winning position? in general no: it must run past the integers); a second draft proving the theorem by well-ordering, with two-player games (win, loss, draw); one page for N players. Then: arranging values to maximize the peak of a convolution on a group. Hua, findings register, **68-orientation-stokes-axioms** (our scans 050, 052; Lean card "holds"; new to us): an orientation theory as a functor Ω to two-element sets, Ω(0) ≃ {±1}, with natural Stokes bijections Ω(V) → Ω(W) for half-spaces bounded by W, changing sign with the opposite half-space. Hua, modernised reading of cote 162-1: no mathematics; nine pages of loans, most lines struck out, a record of how unprinted geometry circulated in the late 1960s.
